lines.st: Today I gave my beer mug to Uncle Carlo downstairs. His memory is so bad that every other week he asks me again which workshop I bought it from.
I never meant to keep it from him, of course, but that workshop's owner refuses to make two identical mugs, and there's nothing I can do about that.
Before I handed the mug over, I asked him for a free drink in exchange. Carlo, beaming all over his face—
Beaming all over his face, he squinted one eye awkwardly, and in an unusually low voice, furtively and a little embarrassed, he asked me:
"What would you like to drink today?"
I must have smiled, because he looked relieved. "So you're feeling better? Then how about a buttered mint-choco hot milk beer, five sugars?"
I said yes, took a thick paper cup from the drink counter, and carried that free drink home.

The sky darkened, and the moonlight fell in through the window, stacking up like sheets of ice. The steam off the drink grew thinner and thinner, yet the room in the moonlight seemed to grow hotter and hotter, and it made me think of that day.
That day, an endless, ardent feeling baked my heart, and like butter in a frying pan, it melted away happily.
A song hummed in my ear as I sipped at the sweet liquid. "La la la, la la..."
"Once upon a time... the rivers... the foothills..."
"Every corner of this earth... I have seen them all..."
"...the salt flats of Iberia... the gravel of Sargon..."
"...the cold winds of Columbia... last year's grass roots..."
"In the taverns of Leithanien... the stomping of dancers never ends..."
"Kazimierz's proud sun is like a blade..."
"In an Ursus spring the snowmelt boils up into kitchen smoke..."
"And at last I came to Laterano..."
"There is no place that compares to Laterano."
"Sugar and guns and faith..."
"I drink Laterano down in one."

lines.x: Delivered! Only twenty minutes late, and we've got the whole morning. Just think of it as getting to look at one more rejected option!
"Getting to look at one more rejected option." I believe that's called wasting time?

I never said it wasn't...
But instead of scolding me why don't we look at the goods first otherwise we'll waste even more time won't we Miss Giada!

...Present them, then, Mr. Giulio. There's no need to show off how fast you can talk. You aren't hosting a party, and I'm not in that much of a hurry.
Given that you say you spent six whole days on this,
I have high expectations.
I know you don't mean that, but that's all right. Let's start with this four-wheel-drive model with the adjustable awning!
I beg your pardon?
Four-wheel drive, driver's seat with an adjustable awning, drivable by anyone twelve and over — the top speed is only twenty-five kilometers an hour, but...
I'd call that a selling point, actually. Any faster and the guests would need a license to drive it.
You were planning to let the guests drive it?

Well, what I had in mind was that guests could sit in the driver's seat and take a photo with Auntie. Wouldn't that look wonderful?
As for whether we open it up for the guests to drive, if you approve of it...

Right, you don't approve, understood!
Next.
A life-size "Cupcake Kid" statue! The dessert brand that I grew up with, and surely Auntie and even Grandma too! And I've confirmed it's properly licensed.
...Fine. I've seen Cupcake Kid-themed caskets before, but usually it's just a printed design. This one of yours...
The artist I had to go through four people to find would never make something mass-produced. This life-size statue model is the only one in existence, and what makes it even more special—
Look, the statue opens up. The interior is contoured to the body, the limbs articulate, and it's remote-controllable and programmable.
If you like, we could have it dance "Vera Jane" on the day. I love that song, and I'm sure Auntie would have—

Right, you wouldn't like that, understood.
Then next...

Oh! Here's the functional design Miss Giada is so fond of — shaped like a food container, and it genuinely keeps things fresh! Built-in Leithanien-made cryo Originium Arts module, four-cycle refrigeration.
The transparent material also makes it easy for Auntie to take photos with the guests! Although given the interior layout, we might have to be selective about which keepsakes go in with her...
Ah, so you do remember we're choosing a casket.
Putting the deceased in a food container, and then the interior layout... What sort of layout, exactly? Are you turning her into a carton of soy milk Sankta?

Great idea!
...I'm guessing that isn't the answer you wanted to hear.
Please, Miss Giada, could you spare a thought for my party? The casket is the centerpiece of the whole venue. The model we pick basically decides the style of the entire party floor. This matters.
First of all, it is a funeral venue, not a party venue. The essence of this rite is the funeral. The party is merely an addition, Mr. Giulio, and we could do without it entirely—
No, no, no, we must have it, and you know it perfectly well — a legally binding will, enforced by the Notarial Hall. An Executor hauled me all the way back from Columbia to Laterano for this.
The Law stands above us, so throwing a proper party at Auntie's funeral is the most important thing in my life!—for this month, at least.
I am not refusing the party. I am saying that, by its nature, a party is not a necessary part of a funeral...

Miss Giada, I know how much this funeral means to you. I know it can't have been easy for a Liberi to become a funeral planner. Before I met you, I didn't even know a Liberi could be a funeral planner—
(Deep breath)
—Sorry! Sorry! I've put my foot in it again, haven't I? Are you angry?

I am not.
And it doesn't matter. I know you need to cook up some... hm... entertaining things.
That's your job. I have no objection.
But I would like Mr. Giulio to understand that the casket and the deceased are first and foremost the heart of the funeral, and only after that are they your... fixtures, on your party stage.

There's no need to look at me so nervously... Yes, this is the first funeral I've handled on my own, but I am a Lateran too. I know what Lateran funerals are like.
Still, there are plenty of rather more... moderate options, aren't there?
For instance, let me see...
This chocolate chip cookie casket is quite nice. No special features either. Don't you think it's just right?

But that's only the popular model the workshop sent over to push on us...
It's your first funeral. Don't you want something a bit more special, Miss Giada?
It isn't my funeral...
Never mind. I don't think we'll reach an agreement on the casket today. Let me get something else straight with you first.
That "guest entrance" you designed earlier—
They slide down a chute into a gift box full of bobo balls, throw the bobo balls into a basket outside, and draw a prize based on how the throws land—
I don't believe I agreed to that?
So why has the gift box already been built?
Giada pointed, exasperation written all over her face, at the cake-shaped gift box sitting in the corner of the prep room — about the size of an inflatable children's pool.
Oh, so you spotted it! I was going to bring it up once the casket was settled. You said you didn't quite follow before, so I was planning to give you a live demonstration—
As if on cue with Giulio's declaration of a "live demonstration," the top of the "cake" suddenly twitched.
...This gift box. Is it motorized?
It shouldn't be... I didn't ask for that when I put the order in with the workshop, and the lid doesn't need to open all that often...
Er, shall I go and take a look...?
But he couldn't take a single step, because Giada had a tight grip on his sleeve and was staring helplessly at that gift box — it was moving again.
The lid, with its delicate piped icing, pushed up once more, then tilted, slid, and dragged out a long, sharp scraping sound...
And then they both saw the hand reaching out of the gift box.
...Where... is this?
Somewhere I don't know... This isn't Tartarus?
Where is everyone...?
The boy who had sat up in the gift box still seemed unwell, frowning as he looked around—
The three of them stared at one another.
...People? No... those are halos... and feathers... aren't they?
...Giulio. Did you arrange this too?
Arrange what? Arrange how? You mean this kid?
No, no, when I said a demonstration I meant I'd get in myself. I'm not so far gone that I'd shut a child in a gift box to, uh... give you a "surprise"!
(An unfamiliar language... and yet I can understand it...)
(Do Shadows in Tartarus... talk?)
Are you all right?
...I'm fine.
Are you an apprentice from the workshop? Did you shut yourself in the gift box by accident? Thank goodness this box isn't airtight...
Come on out first, kid. I'll get you a cup of hot cocoa... er, where's the pantry, Giada?
...Let me get this straight. You're saying your name is Makoto Yuki, you came to Laterano with your friends, you were attacked by beasts outside the city, and when you woke up you were in this box?
(This place... "Laterano," these two people...)
(Until I understand the situation, I should be careful.)
...More or less, yes.
I had a look around, and I didn't see any other kids.
Perhaps the workshop staff rescued him and something went wrong on the way back into the city...
...Excuse me, both of you. There are actually still some things I don't understand.
I came to... "Laterano." I understand that part. But where exactly is this...?
I seem to see a lot of rides. Is this... an amusement park? And the two of you work here...?
This might be a little hard for a foreigner to follow... these things are actually caskets...
...The kind used for funerals?
Yes. This is Laterano's newly built funeral home, and I'm the funeral planner who works here.
As for me, I'm a party designer. At the moment you could say I'm working at the funeral home temporarily.
We really are preparing for a funeral, and today we're choosing a casket for it.
Before we found you, Miss Giada and I were having an argument about exactly that!
An argument?! I was simply discussing work with you!
Arguing isn't good, though...
...I'm sorry. I shouldn't lose my temper in front of a child.

Oho, so you admit you were losing your temper—
Oh, I've got an idea!
Makoto, would you be willing to do us a favor?

In a little while I'm going to try these caskets out myself, and I'd like you to check how they look together with Giada — once I'm lying in one I can't exactly judge it from the viewer's angle, can I!
You look like an honest kid, so you're bound to judge fairly, right—
Giulio, what nonsense are you talking? We should be taking him to the Notarial Hall right away.
Take him straight to the Notarial Hall? He's a foreigner with no proof of identity. The Notarial Hall will deport him within three days.
...And what does that have to do with you asking Yuki for a favor? He isn't even an adult. Even if you had him work alongside us, the funeral home couldn't possibly employ him...

It's not that complicated! It's just a bit of one person helping another—
Makoto, if you're willing to help me...
uh, help us,
I'll tell the Notarial Hall you're a relative of mine. How about it? With a citizen to vouch for you, you can stay.
...Are you teaching an "honest kid" to lie to an Executor?
Twisting a child's arm is a very poor look.
T-twisting his arm?! Hold on, how did you get that out of it? That isn't what I meant at all...
(They look rather unusual... but from the way they talk, those two aren't bad people.)
("Laterano" seems to be the name of some country, though I've never heard of it... If everyone from S.E.E.S. wandered in here too, I need to find them quickly.)
All right. I'll help.
Yuki, you don't have to listen to his nonsense. Even if you'd rather not help, I can vouch for you instead. We'll work the rest out later.
You've both been very kind to me, so if there's anything I can help with, I'd be glad to.
Afterward, could you tell me more about this "Notarial Hall"?
Of course, of course! See, Giada? This is what you call helping each other out.
I'm grateful to you as well, Miss Giada.
The two of you...

All right, all right, Giada, Makoto, shall we get to work? Let me see...
Let's start with the model called "Full Speed to the Holy Spirit"!
Very good... your basic registration is complete. Here is your temporary authentication code and terminal.
Next up, let me see... have you already chosen a school, or will young Yuki choose for himself?
School?
...He's only here visiting family. He has no plans to enroll in Laterano.

I'm afraid that won't do. He isn't an adult yet, and you registered him as having "no plans to leave the country," which means he must be enrolled. It's March right now, so the timing works out nicely.

No problem, no problem at all! Children ought to be in school. Reverend Executor, would you mind letting me see the list of schools?
...Hmm...
Found it!
San Marso Comprehensive School. This one.
...Why did you turn straight to my school?
Hm? This is the school I went to as a kid.
Have you decided? Then I'll enter it. One moment, please.
(Quietly) Wasn't Yuki supposed to be looking for his companions? How is he going to do that while attending school...
(Quietly) After class, obviously. And if all else fails he can skip.
(Quietly) Makoto, you're not the kind of straitlaced student who's afraid to skip class, are you? You could skip and come help out at the funeral home.
(Quietly) I've never skipped class... I just fall asleep in it sometimes.
(Quietly) ...Since you're going to school, you will not skip class. No skipping, and no sleeping through lessons either!
All entered, and the school has confirmed it. He can report in today.
At first I thought this child had come for the funeral. I'd no idea he'd be staying here for a while. I'd never heard that Ms. Vivetta had relatives in Higashi.
...You knew my aunt?
No, only the colleague executing her will. I heard he brought a party designer back from Columbia to hold Ms. Vivetta's funeral... no, her party.
I have been rather curious, actually. That will was registered twenty years ago, which would make Mr. Giulio six at the time. Why would she name you to throw the party at her funeral?
I... I don't remember either.
Excuse me, Reverend Executor, may we go now?
Of course, of course. Best of luck with everything! And do leave me a good review~
The school I'm going to now — is it the one the two of you attended?
It is, ha ha. Quite the coincidence. I never imagined Miss Giada would be an alum too... though I can't picture her in our school uniform at all.
I hardly ever wore it, in fact. I was of the plain-clothes persuasion.
Huh, our school allowed that...?
Did you really attend the same school as me?
I did, I really did. Nearly every kid in the San Marso district goes to that school, don't they? I lived there when I was little.

The main road through San Marso gets the Ecclesia Requietum's hearses passing by all the time. Sit at the roadside and watch, and the feelings of the clerics and the families brush past you in gusts, like wind... don't they?
I suppose they did... Back then, people held funerals at the Ecclesia Requietum whenever the city came to a halt...
What was that sound?
An explosion.
That'll be San Rocco Street. A new cream puff shop opened there and it's very popular.
...You're very calm about it. And that sound just now... was that gunfire?
It was. We're almost at the school.
That student over there is here to meet you, I expect.
Ah, there he is!
Over here!
Hello! Excuse me, are you Makoto Yuki?
After moving to Columbia, I never thought I'd set foot in this school again...
Are you two from Columbia? I've seen a few Columbian films. Is Tkaronto really that dangerous?
Ah, was that a silly question? I suppose Laterans don't ride guns to school either...
Ha ha, compared to Laterano, every city on this earth would have to be called "dangerous."
But that explosion and the gunfire just now...
Ah.
I forgot to explain that to you.
The gunshots? That's the gunnery class. I was at the range myself when the teacher called me over to meet you.
What is a gunnery class... and what was the explosion about...?
That's the cream puff shop's membership event. They change the flavor of the cream puff statue out front every week, and members can enter a draw to blow up last week's statue.
That's how Laterano is. Every explosion is witnessed by an Executor. It isn't dangerous.

Hm... I see. It's your first time in Laterano, Yuki, so there must be a lot you're not used to yet.
If you need help, or if anything puzzles you, you can always come to me or to our teacher.
Thank you, Amiya.
Makoto Yuki, correct? I'm your homeroom teacher, Doctor. You may call me Doctor.
Doctor... sir?
Understood, Doctor.
All right, Doctor.
The hooded teacher pointed to a seat in the second row, in the middle of the classroom.
Your seat is over there.
Take these forms and fill them out. If anything is unclear, ask the class rep — that's Amiya.
Right!
Huh... Sir, Yuki only just arrived. Does he have to fill in the Vocational Placement Form too?
If he doesn't, he'll be stuck at school by himself while the rest of you are out on placement.
(That might not be so bad, actually. I could use the chance to look for everyone.)
Even if he skips the placement he still has to stay at school. The school has a duty of care toward him now.
(This Doctor... does he know what I'm thinking?)
What did you see?
Your face. Students' thoughts are easy to read, so don't look so startled. And there's no need to be formal with me.
...Did I say that out loud?
No. Students' thoughts are simply easy to read. And there's no need to be formal with me.
All right. But what exactly is a "vocational placement"?
Er, Doctor, Makoto grew up abroad and doesn't know how Lateran schools work. Could you explain it for him...
Certainly. Yuki, you've enrolled in the eleventh grade — the first year of prep school — which means your first vocational placement, to prepare you for choosing a career.
Put simply, you write down three lines of work that interest you on this form, and the school arranges a placement at a matching post.
If you fill it in at random, or name work that can't take a placement, the Tribunals' system will reassign you to something close to it.

Though sometimes it's hard to see the logic of the reassignment... Last year an upperclassman wrote down "blazing demolitions maniac" and got assigned to the Notarial Hall.
Surely that isn't what Executors are for...
In any case, today is the deadline. If you want to take part in the placement, you can still finish the form in time.
This child only just arrived in Laterano, and he's been through something frightening. His head must still be in a whirl. Must it be decided this very moment?
It's best decided now.
This question isn't really that hard for you, is it? My guess is that you know perfectly well what you need to do.
(What I need to do right now is... first, find my friends. Which means I need time to move around freely...)
Yes. I understand.
Miss Giada, for the first item on the placement form, may I write "funeral planner"?
And for the second, I'd like to write "party designer working at a funeral home."
(Quietly) Please... and if there's anything you need me to do, I'll do my best to help.
...You really are a bit of a headache, you know that?
You need three entries. What do you intend to put for the last one?
Doctor, or Amiya — do you have any suggestions?
The most commonly chosen job is shop assistant at the Confectionery Hall. If you'd rather not stand out.
The Confectionery Hall is a bit like a market, except everything they sell is sweets. I put that down too, so if you pick it, we might get placed together.

All right, then I'll put Confectionery Hall shop assistant for the last one.
That's everything filled in...
No, wait, there's another sheet?
A Dormitory Application Form...
Hardly any local students ever apply for the dormitory, but given your situation I brought one along anyway.
Well then, Makoto Yuki. Will you be taking a dorm room?
Ooh, it's my first time in the school dorms. Not bad at all! Though there doesn't seem to be anyone about...?
Right, very few students applied for the dorms — almost everyone at school is local.
Actually, if Makoto would rather stay with me, that's also—
Says the man still living in the Returnees' Apartments.
The dorm is fine for me. I'm used to it.

Your room is on the second floor, Yuki. You can change the passcode from your terminal.
Um... will your luggage be coming later?
Luggage...
Shouldn't we buy him some daily necessities? Now that he's enrolled, he ought to have what he needs.
You've turned into a proper guardian...
Go on home and rest, Amiya. You can leave the rest to us.
All right, I'll head back to school then.
It's nearly the end of the school day. You're not going straight home?
I'm going to walk our teacher home after work!
Miss Giada, Mr. Giulio, thank you very much for today.
And I'm counting on you both for the placement.
Hah. What you mean is, you'd like the two of us to look the other way during your placement so you can go looking for your friends. Am I right?
Saying it out of nowhere like that made me stop and think. And here I was hoping Makoto had actually taken an interest in funerals after working with us...
But you're still hiding something from us, aren't you, Yuki?
If you want to find your friends... why not let us report it to an Executor?
(I'm almost certain now. This isn't the world I came from... The cities, the countries, the names of the peoples — I've never heard any of them.)
(Judging by what happened at the Notarial Hall, Laterano seems to have strict laws and rules...)
(I managed to gloss over where I really came from for now, but if an Executor investigates in earnest... there's no telling how Laterano would treat people in our situation.)
Did the talk of deportation earlier frighten you?
...I will go home. Once I've found my friends.
But... I'd like to look for them under my own power first. Would that be all right?
Of course it would.
Didn't you answer a little too quickly?
Were you going to refuse?
If I really can't find any leads...
The boy's words were cut off by a chorus of shrieks growing nearer, tangled up with shouts of confusion and delight.
All three of them turned toward it. Giulio rose on his toes to peer in the direction of the noise, while Giada frowned and motioned for Yuki to stand back.
The cries rose and fell, closer and closer, along with faint apologies and the slap of running feet. Something made Makoto step toward the roadside...
A gray shape came barreling straight at him—
Woof! Awooo—
Koromaru, slow down, slow down! Where even is this? I don't think we're in Tartarus...
Is this a main street...? And the people on it... are they human? How strange...
Koromaru! Why are you speeding up? Don't tell me you've found—
Makoto?!
Makoto... is that you?
Koromaru, and Ken...!
Thank goodness... Koromaru really did find you!
Yuki...?
Yes, these are my friends... two of them. This is Ken Amada, and the other one is... named Koromaru.
...Hello?
Awoof awoof!
Ahaha, well, at least we hadn't bought the daily necessities yet. Saves us a second trip...
(Quietly) Giulio, is that... a beckbeast?
(Quietly) ...More like a Perro Beast Steward? Hm... do Perro Beast Stewards eat beckbeast feed?
Woof?
...All right. I've been in touch with Yuki's teacher, so Ken can stay in the dorms starting tonight. We'll register him at the Notarial Hall and the school later.
Ahaha... another cousin for the collection...
Makoto, why don't you tell us a little about your friends in advance? How many of you there are, for instance...?
So I know how many relatives I'm supposed to have.

Counting me, the ones who came with me on this trip—
the ones who came to Laterano with me should be five. Plus Koromaru.
So... Giada, shall we split them between us?
...We don't have to pass every one of them off as a relative. Registering them as friends of a citizen's family should do.
(Quietly) Makoto, what on earth is going on...?
(Shakes his head slightly)
Let's do as Miss Giada says.
Then... thank you so much, really!
Woof!
You must be exhausted after today. Get some rest, both of you.
Huh? Can't we sit a while longer? I'm tired too...
This is a student dormitory.

All right, all right...
I'll come see you again. Bye for now!
...Ken, Koromaru, let's talk in my room.
Sure!/Arf!
Giulio.
What else can I do for you, Miss Giada?
...I'll say it plainly. Aren't you taking Yuki's side rather too much?
I was going to say you were coddling him, but having this conversation with you is strange enough as it is... You aren't his real cousin, and we aren't his real guardians.
Do you think Yuki's a bad kid? There's no need to be on guard against him.
I'm not saying we should be on guard. But don't you trust people rather too easily?
Wasn't it Giada who said she'd vouch for him even if he didn't help us?
All he wants is to find his friends. I haven't felt the slightest trace of ill will from that boy all day.
He isn't a Sankta. And besides, you're currently—
What does being a Sankta have to do with it? I don't understand what you're so worried about... Why think that far ahead?
I have a funeral to run. Frankly, you turning up was already quite enough to deal with...
...Fine, fine, I understand. You don't want me meddling in the first funeral you're responsible for. I've grasped that thoroughly over these past few days. There's no need to keep hammering it home.
But this is Auntie's will. Let me see it through, and after that I won't have any more chances to bother you, Miss Giada.
Oh. You make that same face every time I mention "Auntie's will."
Of course, I'm not her closest nephew — I'm a second cousin's nephew, and after my parents divorced I never saw that distant great-aunt of mine again.
But even if it were just an ordinary client's commission, I'd still want to give them the best party I possibly could, with my whole heart.
Miss Giada, can you understand that I have my own principles too...? Though I honestly don't know why I'm explaining all this.
Nor do I. I shouldn't have brought the subject up. I need to go and confirm the casket arrangements.
What's left to confirm? Didn't Makoto end up choosing the casket you liked today?
...Choosing the model isn't the end of it. Transport, the encoffining, reservations for each of the funeral home's facilities...
Never mind. Why am I explaining, again. I'll send you the parts you need to know. Good night.
...Good night, Miss Giada.
...So what you're saying is, we might not be in our own world anymore. We're in a country called Laterano.
And living here are "Sankta," with "halos" over their heads, and "Liberi," who have feathers...
Halos over their heads — could they be angels...? But is there any record anywhere of angels all carrying guns...?
If this isn't our world to begin with, the Sankta may have nothing to do with the "angels" we know...
True... Still, we're lucky we can talk to them without any trouble.
We and the "humans" here look more or less alike... and their way of life doesn't seem all that different either.
They have shops and schools and so on here as well...
You've been observing very closely, Ken.
N-not really! It's a strange world, so when I see something familiar I can't help noticing it...
Come to think of it, this city isn't small. I didn't expect you to find me so quickly.
That's all thanks to Koromaru! He followed your scent, and that's how we found you.
When I woke up, Koromaru and I were already in Laterano... I was a bit confused at the time, and it took me a while to catch up.
It was a while before it slowly came back to me. We'd set out from the dorm and gone to Tartarus...
That's how I remember it too. You, me, Fuuka, Yukari, Aigis and Koromaru — we went to investigate Shadows the way we always do.
I don't remember anything unusual on the way to Tartarus... but once we were inside, we found a door on the first floor that had appeared out of nowhere.
I remember we went over to take a look at it, but I don't remember anything after we got close to it...
At least Akihiko, Mitsuru and Junpei had other things on and didn't come exploring this time. Otherwise every one of us would have been dragged in...
Yes... If they find out we're missing, they'll be terribly worried. We need to get back as soon as we can.
If we came here through that door... maybe we can go back by finding the same door?
That's what I thought too, and I already looked around the funeral home...

The "funeral home"...
Ah, that's where you woke up, isn't it? That's where you met Miss Giada and Mr. Giulio...
Yes, I spent the whole morning working there with them... Come to think of it, we didn't find you at the funeral home.
Ken, where did you and Koromaru wake up?

Where we woke up was... inside a vehicle.
It was a vehicle, but the inside looked like a confessional booth, so at first I thought we were indoors...
Then I opened the door and Koromaru and I nearly fell out while it was still moving. Luckily it stopped in time. And the vehicle actually talked — it said its name was "the confessional"...
It even said goodbye to us very politely...
When we got out we were on a main street, but the passersby looked a bit odd, so I didn't dare speak to them.
Then it occurred to me that I could ask Koromaru to track everyone's scent, and maybe we'd all meet up... and that's how we found you, Makoto.
I see... We went through the same door, but we woke up in different places. That's strange.
But doesn't that mean Fuuka, Yukari and Aigis might be in different places as well...
...That does seem very likely. Should we ask Koromaru to track their scent after all?
Awoo...
Koromaru... don't tell me you didn't pick up any trace of them on the way?
Woof...
...So it seems.
Hmm...
I was thinking... could it be that Yukari and the others haven't arrived in Laterano yet?
We still don't know how that door works, of course...
But I remember that from when Koromaru and I woke up to when we found you, it can't have been more than an hour...
And you just said you worked at the funeral home all morning, didn't you...
That's right. Which means that although we went through the door at the same time, I appeared in Laterano earlier than you did.
Exactly! So I think the reason Koromaru couldn't pick up their scent might be that Yukari and the others haven't shown up in Laterano yet...
We definitely all went through that door that appeared in Tartarus together, and then we ended up here...
If what's behind the door is a passage connecting the two worlds, and Yukari and the others haven't arrived yet, could they still be inside the door right now...?
Then it's all the more important that we find that door.
So that we can find everyone and go back to our world together.
But where the door is... Maybe we should go back near that "funeral home" and look again?
I've searched that area pretty thoroughly. If a door like that had appeared out of thin air, it would have drawn a lot of attention.
But neither Giulio nor Giada has ever mentioned anything like it. And no "door" appeared where I woke up, either...
That's so strange. Can the door turn invisible too?
Though nothing that's happened so far can really be explained by common sense either...
Right. If we can meet up with Fuuka later, maybe we can use her Persona's power to find some kind of clue...
And if Koromaru picks up anything, we can send him out again! He found you, so I'm sure he can find Fuuka and the others too.
Woof!

Koromaru's raring to go!
But we can't search right now, can we — it's late...
Meaning to check the time, Makoto looked up at the clock on the wall — and suddenly realized something.
The time...
Ken followed his gaze. The twelve-hour face, under the soft click of the second hand, was familiar in a way that felt almost wrong.
...It's almost midnight! The Dark Hour—
The Dark Hour: the "hidden time" that exists in the world Makoto and his friends come from.
A "time outside of time" that arrives every night at midnight, and the hour when the monsters called Shadows roam unchecked.
During it the world falls still, yet ordinary people notice nothing, and have no power to resist even as the Shadows harm them.
Only those "who carry a special power," like Makoto and his companions, can move within the Dark Hour and stand against the Shadows.
The "Specialized Extracurricular Execution Squad" — S.E.E.S. — that Makoto and his friends formed at Gekkoukan High School exists precisely to investigate the Dark Hour and destroy the Shadows.
...Will there be a Dark Hour in Laterano?
The hands of the clock moved silently onward.
...It seems not. Time went on as normal...
Both of them let out a breath at the same moment. And yet...
It was then that Koromaru turned his head toward the window.
Woof woof—!!!
Awoo... woof!!
Koromaru?
Koromaru, did you find something?
Woof!
Then let's go. Koromaru, lead the way.
The street doesn't look any different...
Koromaru, what is it you found...
Awoo! Arf!
Nothing seems out of the ordinary here either...
How can this be? Is this... the Dark Hour?
...But the clock in the square is still running, isn't it?
Mm... I don't think this is the Dark Hour.
Look.
Makoto, is there something over there...
Huh! Once we walk this far, the street is back to normal...
Yes. And from here you can't see what was over there just now.
What is this... a localized "Dark Hour"?
In any case, let's investigate a little more.
Woof!
Awoo—woof woof!
Over there!
In the eerie night, a familiar girl was fighting something none of them had ever seen before...
...A Shadow?
Koromaru leapt in and drove back the Shadow-like creature behind her.
Is that... Koromaru?
Woof woof!
Yukari!
Yuki...! And Ken!
Yukari's attention wavered for just an instant, and the Shadow slipped past her arrow and closed the distance fast.
Yukari, look out!
The Shadow closing on Yukari scattered under the group's attacks, and an eerie flash appeared again a little way off. Yukari and Makoto exchanged a glance.
Makoto nodded in understanding, and Yukari sprang lightly onto the plinth of a roadside statue of a saint to look toward the flash.
Makoto picked up the arrow that had fallen from the Shadow's dissolving body and tossed it up to Yukari, perched beside the statue.
Her fingers swept across it and the arrow settled onto the rest. Yukari focused and held her breath, and the instant the Shadow came into effective range she drew and loosed in one clean motion—
Save me, oh save me—♪
An off-key song broke the quiet. A swaying figure came out of an alley onto the street, stopping right in front of the Shadow.
Makoto reacted faster than Yukari's cry of alarm. He knocked the arrow down, but there was no stopping the drunken Sankta from walking straight into the Shadow.
The Shadow seemed to spread its arms, and for a moment the Sankta's form was swallowed entirely inside it.
And then the Sankta passed through the Shadow, as though passing through air.
He looked without seeing and heard without listening, staggering onward, drunkenly singing his tuneless song.

lines.st: "...Save me, I can't face this life alone♪"

lines.x: He seemed entirely unharmed, except for that halo growing dimmer and dimmer. The street corner he had briefly lit sank back into the night.

lines.st: "I cry at night, and still I want to believe your lies♪"

lines.x: The Shadow he had passed through came no farther, standing stock-still behind the Sankta, almost as if... watching him.

lines.st: "Save me, I'm already stripped bare with nothing left...♪"

lines.x: Yukari could see more Shadows welling up from the end of the street. She reached instinctively for the quiver at her back. It was empty.
Everyone, I'm here to back you up!
A gentle call carried from a distance, and in the dimmed night Yukari caught sight of a familiar figure.
The short-haired girl raised the Evoker in her hand and leveled it at herself. Even from so far away, the resolve in her eyes seemed visible.
Through the discolored street rang a call full of determination.
Juno — carry this prayer!
Awoo...?!
That voice... Fuuka!
Fuuka, that's a huge help.
—Everyone, let's go!
Phew... I'm glad I made it in time.
Fuuka, thank goodness, you're safe! It's lucky you got here when you did...
Thank goodness... everyone's all right...
But the one lying over there... is he a passerby? Is he... singing?
...I love you... until...♪
Hooh... hooh...
Is he... asleep?
It looks like it. He's curled up, but I don't see any sign of injury...
But this thing above his head... his halo? It's gone very dark. There's almost no light left in it.
Can this guy really not see Shadows? He walked right into that one's arms just now, didn't he?
It does look that way... And once all the Shadows were destroyed, the strange area disappeared. So this... isn't the Dark Hour?
It shouldn't be. Makoto and I checked — time wasn't stopped.
Not the Dark Hour... Then what are these Shadows?
And where on earth is this? Why are you all so calm, Yuki? It's like you already know something...
I was wondering about that too... At first I couldn't understand it — could there be a space like this inside Tartarus? Something felt off.
And for some reason I couldn't sense any of you...
Searching with Juno's power didn't go well either, which felt very strange... There's been a constant interference, like static. No matter what I did, I couldn't sense where anyone was...
But in the end I finally picked up something like Shadow activity, and when I rushed over and found you all here, I was so relieved...
Yeah. The moment I woke up I ran into Shadows I'd never seen before, and I've been fighting ever since... You showing up really saved me.
If this isn't Tartarus, then where is it? Judging by the streets, it doesn't look like Iwatodai either...
...It seems we've come to another world.
A-another world?!
Yes. This city is called "Laterano," and the people living here aren't the same kind of humans as us...
People with halos and wings of light like these are called "Sankta," and there also seems to be a people called "Liberi."
I don't know much more than that myself yet...
Let's go back to the dorm and talk it through. Oh, and...
The dorm...?
Huh, why did Yuki take out a phone? Do phones even work here...?
That's not right — I don't remember Yuki's phone looking like that... Never mind, let's just leave it to him.
Doctor, sorry to disturb you. There's something I'd like to ask of you.
...Now then, Amiya, this is Yukari Takeba and Fuuka Yamagishi, who enrolled today. Introduce yourselves, then go and collect their textbooks and uniforms.
Huh...? When school let out yesterday there was only Yuki... foreign transfer students... and today there are two more?
The transfer student Q&A booklet I made last night... isn't enough...!
Please wait a moment, I need to run to the copy room...
So this is the class rep Yuki mentioned? It's fine, we'll just ask you directly if we have questions.
Shall we swap contacts?
Yukari... you're amazing...
You too, Yamagishi. Here's my authentication code.

Authentication code... ah, the terminal account number.
All right, here's mine.
Anyway, we're in the same year, so just call me Yukari. Fuuka prefers being called by name too, right?
Mm-hm. Being too formal makes me a little nervous...
Sure! Are Fuuka and Yukari friends of Yuki's as well?
Yes. We go to the same school back home.
I see... You must be very close, to travel to Laterano together.
Oh, sir, about Fuuka and Yukari's vocational placement... is there still time?
You must know a way, sir. Otherwise they'll have to stay at school by themselves, and that's just too lonely...
...I'll ask a friend at the Tribunals. They'll probably have to join the same placement as Yuki. Is that acceptable?
That's fine. Yuki told us about the placement.
Though... can an elementary schooler take part in this "vocational placement"? See, I have a little brother...

opts: He can if he skips ahead to middle school.

lines.x: Sir... can't he?
Sir, Yukari is asking seriously. Please don't tease people...
Very well.
It isn't difficult, really. You only want to be able to move around together during the placement. You aren't after placement credit and a certificate for this elementary schooler, are you?
That's right.
Elementary schoolers can't take part in the placement, and students taking part in the placement can't take leave — which means an elementary schooler not taking part in the placement can take leave.
And where he spends that leave is his own business.
Huh... it can be that simple?
Life in Laterano is a life of understanding rules, Amiya. The point of a rule is not to restrict but to clarify. Many Laterans understand the first half of that, but not yet the second.
Do you have to put it so cryptically, sir...
I think I understand. Thank you, Doctor.
You understand? All the better. Knowing a little more about the world is very useful — for you especially.
Every student picks three posts for their placement, completed over three days. For you lot it will likely be one day at the Confectionery Hall and two at the Ecclesia Requietum Funeral Home.
When the schedule comes through, remember to check your terminals. That goes for all of you, Amiya included.
Until then, attend your classes properly. If you skip, I will know.
A buttered hazelnut latte, Miss Giada! Only two pumps of syrup — Perla said you don't like things too sweet.
...Is this your apology?
Hm? Surely I'm not the one who should be apologizing. Wasn't it Giada who left me standing there in the cold yesterday?
I don't like nuts.
Wha—
I'm teasing. Mm. It's not bad.
Actually, I came to discuss the layout of the funeral venue. Now that the casket model is settled...
I'm quite certain your idea of it and mine are nothing alike, but — shall we talk it over anyway? We might find something that works both ways. You'd be happy and I'd be happy.
...Happy? I don't come to work to be happy...
Is that so bad? Miss Giada clearly loves her work. I can tell!
I'm a funeral planner. Being happy about my work would hardly be appropriate.

...I didn't mean it literally! I only wanted to...
Haah. I said the wrong thing before. When I said I'd never seen a Liberi funeral planner, what I meant was that I admire you...
I actually asked Perla about it just now... I hear you saved a funeral that had gone off the rails?
...Hardly. Scenes like that weren't rare at all, for a while there. I simply... it was simply that, on that one occasion, something I could do occurred to me.
May I hear about it?
...The deceased at that funeral was a comic actor. His family and his colleagues decided to restage the piece that had made his name as a young man, as a tribute.

The performance really was splendid, and plenty of the guests laughed out loud. But the deceased's wife suddenly broke down. In tears, she rushed the stage and demanded that the performer — his colleague — stop at once.
The performer stopped, but his awkwardness drew another round of laughter. The wife's grief turned to fury, and red-eyed, she demanded to know what all these guests took her husband for.
...What an awful scene...
That sort of thing wouldn't have happened before, would it?
So what did you... do?

I asked the two of them to come down from the stage to the casket, and asked whether they would each choose a sweet for him to set before it. The wife chose a meringue; the colleague, a raspberry cookie.

Then I asked everyone to do the same in turn — to think back on what they had shared with him and choose a sweet for him. Or simply choose one they liked themselves, and recommend it to him. That was fine too.
At the very least, everyone grew calm. Some, after setting down their sweet, bent over and said a few words to him that no one else could catch.
You're so clever...
It has nothing to do with being clever. I simply understood... that in that moment, nobody knew what they were supposed to do. They didn't even know what they were supposed to feel.
I simply understood how unbearable that is.
...Right. It wasn't like this before.
Unable to feel others, and unable to let others feel us...
So you're afraid I'll make a dreadful scene like that happen all over again?
If you people insist on making merry at a funeral, that is exactly what happens.
...Miss Giada, do you think a funeral has to be a sorrowful occasion? But at Lateran funerals there have always been people laughing out loud.
I know. You never used to need a rite to guide your feelings. The feelings came first. Even if you carried on at a funeral, you would be "understood."
But it's different now. Otherwise, why would a Liberi be able to work as a funeral planner at all?
...Do you want to change us, Miss Giada?
You have already changed.
All of us have already changed.
Then... shouldn't we hold on to some things that don't change?
Not daring to laugh, or not being allowed to, just because it's a funeral — even though that's what we've always done. Not even then?
Is that what you think Laterano ought to become?
You're overstating it. I only mean to be accountable for the work in my hands. I have no intention of standing here speculating about Laterano's future with you.
Is that really what you think? Because it doesn't seem to me that you—
You cannot feel how I feel. And allow me to remind you, you never could. I'm delighted to tell you that even without "understanding" one another the way your kind does, I can do my job well.
I— I'm sorry. I didn't mean it that way.
...I'll give the venue layout some more thought. I'll come find you later.
Phew... I'm worn out... Elementary school math here is this hard...
You're so diligent, Ken. I could barely concentrate in class. I kept thinking about how we're going to get back to our world...
Hehe. Still, I understand how Ken feels... The teacher is explaining it so earnestly that not listening properly feels rude...
What about you, Leader?
I thought I could learn about this world from the lessons, so I listened properly.
True, class is part of gathering information too.
And some of the lessons are quite interesting. History class here sounds like a fantasy story — red dragons, pegasus knights...
And "Originium Arts" is basically magic... though I get the feeling that's not something you can learn just by sitting in class.
Woof!
You think so too, don't you, Koromaru?
Oh, Koromaru's wearing something new...!
Yes... Koromaru caught a crocheted table mat that fell out of the activity room window, and this was the owner's thank-you gift...
Koromaru's so popular. By the end of today the whole school seemed to know about "the Beast Steward transfer student." Somebody even wanted to shoot a poster of him...

Hehe, that's our Koro...
Still, sitting around talking in the dorm like this feels a little lonely... with just the few of us.
Yeah... I wonder how Mitsuru and Akihiko are doing. And that idiot Junpei...
And Aigis... She went through the door with us, and we still haven't found a trace of her...
Koromaru doesn't seem to have caught Aigis's scent either...
And on my end, maybe because of the static, I haven't sensed anything like Aigis's presence either...
Speaking of which, Makoto and I talked about it. Even though we all went through the same door, the time and place we arrived in Laterano seem to be different for each of us...
I noticed that too. Yesterday, Yukari and I didn't appear in Laterano until nighttime, but Ken and Koromaru arrived in the afternoon, and our leader in the morning...
Ah, the times really are different. So neither Fuuka nor Koromaru can find Aigis because she might not have entered Laterano yet — is that what you mean?
That's what I think too.
And there's another problem now.
You mean how to get back to our world, right? Since we all went through that door that appeared out of nowhere, and ended up here...
Yes. So I've been thinking — if we can enter that door again in this world, maybe we can get back.
But the time and place the door appears aren't fixed... are they? If we all came out of that door into Laterano...
That's our guess, anyway.
If that's the case, then when Aigis appears, the door would appear too... Could that happen?
It's possible...
But none of us saw a door when we woke up. Even if we did come out of one, it may not stay for long... It might have vanished before we woke.
Could we find that door with Juno's power?
If you could sense where the door is and we chased it down, wouldn't that find Aigis and our way home at the same time?
Yukari has a point. Let me try...
Fuuka summoned Juno and focused on the presences around her, but slowly her brow furrowed all the same.
...Sorry, it doesn't seem to work. There's still that... interference, like static.
It was the same last night before we met up, when I tried to sense everyone. In the end I could barely pick up anything but something like a Shadow's presence...
If that static went away, I might be able to try looking for the door with Juno's power, but as things are...
I see...
It's all right. There may be another way. We can ask around about the door later.
Actually, speaking of Shadows... something from last night has been bothering me.
Do you all remember the way that drunk passerby got "embraced" by that Shadow? Honestly, that image left me uneasy...
We gave him a quick look after the fight and he didn't seem to be hurt...
But being attacked by a Shadow can give you Apathy Syndrome, right? If that happened, it'd be bad...
Mm. If Laterans start getting Apathy Syndrome too, that would be terrible...
What I've been wondering is, if Laterano has no Dark Hour, why are there Shadows at all? Could those Shadows have come here through that door, the same as us...
Shadows coming to Laterano through the door... Well, we don't understand how that door works, so we can't say it's impossible...
Mm... If they really did appear here through the door, then maybe...
Like I said, I can still manage to sense the Shadows' presence. If they're coming out of the door, maybe we can use that to find it...
Really? Then we're not completely without a lead... That's a relief.
Yeah... though right now, all we know about those Shadows is that they might be connected to the door.
Yes. However you look at it, we need to keep investigating those Shadows.
And if Laterans are being drawn into it, and could even be put in danger because of it...
Then maybe we should borrow the strength of the people of this world after all.
Should we report it to the Executors? They're something like police, right...
That's true, but given our situation... I'm not sure they'd believe us. I think it might be better to talk it over first with the people who've already helped us.
And besides, we are students, after all.
Well then. You said there was something "very important" you hoped I'd keep secret. You can say it here.
(Whoa... not being able to see the Doctor's face really is unnerving...)
Ahem... Doctor, I'm sorry for troubling you late last night, and thank you very much for letting Yukari and Fuuka stay at the dorm.

Lucky I hadn't gone to bed, or I might not have taken your call...
Ah — don't tell Amiya I was up all night.
In return, I won't ask how you conjured up two hometown classmates in the small hours.
...I can tell you about that, Doctor.
Go ahead.
We aren't Laterans, and moreover...
Nor are you from Higashi. And that Sankta cousin in your file has nothing to do with you either.
Yes. My friends and I come from another world. If I'm not mistaken.
I see.
You really aren't surprised, Doctor...
Not particularly. I simply didn't want to look into it too closely before.
But since you're volunteering it, you must have run into trouble... You want to go home, and you can't find the way?
That's part of it... but the main reason we came to you is that we've found out Laterans may be in danger.
A monster called a "Shadow," which exists in the world we come from... seems to have appeared in Laterano as well.
In our world, we're actually members of an organization that fights Shadows — the Specialized Extracurricular Execution Squad, S.E.E.S.
If we can, we'd like to return to our own world in the way that involves the fewest people and draws the least attention.
But if the Shadows are going to harm Laterano, we aren't willing to stand by and watch it happen.
...Tell me in detail. About "Shadows," and about yourselves.
...That's roughly all of it.
"Personas," "Shadows," "Apathy Syndrome"... I see...
If there's any part you'd like to know more about, Doctor, please ask. Everyone can help answer.

opts: There is more I'd like to ask.
No need, I understand it all.

Let me think of something.

Ah, y-yes, that's me... Thank you.
