Yes. As things stand, we can't leave it alone.
Then, tonight only, I'll go with you. I'd like to see how you fight... and to confirm this matter of "Laterans being unable to see Shadows."
As for whether Apathy Syndrome has appeared in Laterano, I'll look into that myself afterward.
There's also a companion of ours named "Aigis" whom we haven't found. We'd very much like to find her soon...
I can ask around for you. Broadly, I agree with your thinking about the door.
Though the name "Aigis" sounds rather unlike the rest of yours...
If she had already entered Laterano, I would have heard about it. It's quite possible she hasn't appeared here yet.
By your current reasoning, if you can pass through that door again, you may be able to return to your own world.
If you act on the premise that "the Shadows entered Laterano through the door," you may be able to work backward from their movements to locate it.
And even if the door moves, witnessing the moment it appears might give you a clue about how it works...
Let's treat that as the hypothesis to test next.
One other thing that strikes me as suspicious is the "static" Yamagishi described. But too many things could cause that, so for now it can only be a secondary line of research... of investigation.
So, let's proceed along the lines just discussed and investigate the Shadows' activity. Yuki, you're the leader of S.E.E.S., correct?
Yes, I am.
Then lead your squad well, and begin the investigation.
(Yawn) Haah... I'm so sleepy...
With no Dark Hour, investigating at night in Laterano means time just keeps running, so it really does turn into an all-nighter... and the Shadows keep coming, too...
Yeah, I'm a bit sleepy as well... At least the Doctor sent us back to the dorm to rest once he had enough information, so I did get some sleep...
The Doctor also said we still have to pay attention in class during the day. I'd better be careful not to nod off...
Huh, didn't you check the timetable, Yukari? I think this morning is an outdoor class...
"Not a Gun, But Better"... Is that a class on how to use guns...?
Hard to say.
Almost every Sankta on the street carries a gun. They don't seem to be just ornaments...
Though thanks to that, nobody pays any attention to our Evokers.
Mm... Come to think of it, is everyone carrying their Evoker right now?
I am.
I am... There's no Dark Hour here, so there's no telling when Shadows will appear. I thought it was safer to have it...
Oh good, I'm not the only one...
Good morning! What are you talking about?

Morning. We were talking about... this morning's class.
"Not a Gun, But Better" — we couldn't quite make sense of the name...
Oh, the "Non-Gun" class. Let me think how to explain it...
Um... Now that you're in Laterano, you'd all want to learn about gunnery, right? But gunnery is very hard to learn, so the school set up a "Non-Gun" class specially for non-Sankta students.

The Non-Gun class and the gunnery class run together, and together they're called "Gun-Adjacent Armaments." The main difference is the equipment used, and the teachers coach the two groups separately.
If you want to try gunnery, that's fine too. It's just that for non-Sankta students, really mastering it is far too difficult...
Besides gunnery, I really recommend the grenade launcher. Letting loose with it feels great, and it's much easier to pick up.
...Amiya? What are you talking about... letting loose with what?
They actually use real guns in school classes... Seeing it with my own eyes is still a bit of a shock...
Mm... Actually, I'm rather interested... A gun is a kind of machine too, so it might be really interesting...
Fuuka, you really are... I don't know whether to call you tough-minded or just endlessly curious...
I understand how Fuuka feels. The guns here aren't like the ones we use — they're real weapons... A chance to learn about them doesn't come along often.
I'm back. I asked Ms. Carla, and although the basics were covered a while ago, you're transfer students, so she says a little special treatment is fine.
So you're the new foreign transfer students in Doctor's class. Have you had any experience with gunnery before?
Probably not.
"Probably"? Why say "probably"?
Oh? It looks like you're carrying guns yourselves...
...These Evokers only resemble guns on the outside. Would you like to check them?
...The resemblance really is close, but these aren't guns. If you all use staves like these, you must be Casters trained in the same kind of Originium Arts.
(Quietly) Yukari, would summoning a Persona count... as Originium Arts? From what the other teachers have said, Originium Arts is an ability something like magic, right?
(Quietly) It's probably... not quite the same? But I don't know how to explain it to her, so let's just gloss over it for now...
Yes, that's right, more or less... just as you said. It's only that back home we might call it something different.

If you're Casters, then it's certainly worth a try. Which kind of Originium Arts do you use? If it's the Incantation-Transmutation school or the Energy-Shaping school, gunnery should be easier to grasp.
I mean Arts that let you manipulate objects — move them or change their shape — or fire off currents, fireballs, energy beams and the like.
None of those, really...
All right, let's just get a feel for the guns first. Pick one you like and I'll walk you through how to hold it.
If you want to know how the different guns compare, you can ask Vannini — her family runs a gunsmithing workshop. Amiya, go and call Vanni over, would you?
Sure~
...And last, the sniper gun. Longest range, and the recoil is, large. The stock has to, brace against your shoulder... you can, adjust, the length, here.
Which one, do you like?
(Picks up a small gun)
It looks a lot like your Evokers, so it feels familiar? That's a good start.
Come, stand here. Keep the muzzle away from people, and try raising it.
Drop your shoulders. Keep your index finger off the trigger for now — straighten it along the side of the gun.
Your arms are too tense.
Amiya, come here and show Yuki how to hold his arms.
Yuki, you can bend your elbow a little here. It cushions the recoil and keeps you more flexible!
...Your toes, should point, toward the target.
Don't grip, so tightly... Left hand, a little higher, pressing down on your right.
Yuki, are you holding your breath? You don't need to right now — just relax.
Your eyes, don't close them. Keep the eye that isn't on the sight, open too.
Good, your stance is perfect!
Now, feel the Originium circuits in the gun and in the round. Can you connect them?
Oh dear...
Same as us...
It's all right, put the gun down. This is perfectly normal. Non-Sankta usually have some difficulty understanding how a gun fires.
Is it simple for Sankta?
It's rather different. Sankta hardly need to "understand" the structure of a gun's circuits at all. The way we communicate with a gun is closer to empathy...
Haah. To be honest, I'm a little worried. This year's seventh-graders are handling guns for the first time, and they're progressing noticeably slower than in past years.
But in the end they all managed it, didn't they? With a little patience, children always get there.
Adnachiel, what brings you here? Do you have a class with the lower years today?
Ha ha, I'm only helping out for a bit at the Doctor's request. He mentioned there were new students in the gunnery class today, so I came to have a look.
This is Adnachiel, one of Doctor's former students. He isn't a teacher, but his talent is remarkable, and he's very good at guiding students.
I'm just a "crooked halo"...
An aberrant halo, and yet you refuse to join the Lateran, and now you can't even use a gun. I don't understand you.
I find the crossbow rather good, you know? Settling the course of your whole life early just because of the shape of a halo would be quite a waste.
Let's not talk about me. These would be Yuki, Takeba and Yamagishi. How far have you gotten?
"Feel the Originium circuits"... That's where we got stuck.
Still, it sounds like we don't absolutely have to master gunnery, is that right?
Of course not. Whether or not you can use a gun doesn't define a person. Even here in Laterano.
Then I'm going to try that bow over there. Ms. Carla, may I?
Of course you may. Yuki, Yamagishi, would you like to try a Non-Gun weapon as well?
Um... yes please! Actually, I've been wanting to try the grenade launcher Amiya mentioned.
A grenade launcher?! Fuuka, you really are going for the outrageous option...
Ahaha... It's not something you can get your hands on normally, and a chance like this is rare...
No more running! We're in the same group. Run again and I'll treat you like game and drag you back to the range!
Have mercy — guns, bows, crossbows, I'm not interested in any of them! Can't I spend that time drawing in the activity room...

No. If you keep skipping, our group's ranking stays low, and it'll be a pain when that person asks about it...
Don't you dare run again!
Class is nearly over, but isn't it dangerous for those two to chase each other around like that...?
It's fine. Stitch knows the school buildings inside out. He won't run anywhere dangerous.
Is class ending already? I wanted to look at this launcher a bit more...
If you like it, Fuuka, you can come after school too. There's a public range in town as well, so you can go on days off.
It's lucky you don't have to sit the Gun Use Accord exam. Otherwise you'd have loads of make-up classes and live-fire practice — you really would have to spend your days off at the range...
I've been wanting to ask — is everything used in class really live ammunition...?

It is. The eleventh- and twelfth-grade gunnery classes are all live-fire practice, actually. You have to fire thirteen thousand six hundred live rounds under lawful supervision within two years to qualify on graduation.
L-live rounds, really... I think I understand that it's a Lateran custom, but it still feels a little frightening...
It's quite natural to feel that way, Yukari. Most people visiting Laterano for the first time find it strange.
I once met a tourist from Ursus who was frightened out of her wits by gunfire going off beside an ice cream machine...
I can understand that. Although I'm starting to get used to this side of Laterano... There's a range on the way back to the dorm, and it's lively every single day.

Yes. To a Lateran, that kind of "liveliness" feels like home.
If one day the gunfire vanished from the streets entirely... that would probably be the frightening thing.
Makoto, I heard you had a gunnery class today. Was it interesting?
Quite interesting. Though I didn't manage it.
None of us did... The "guns" here seem far more complicated than firearms back home. Without understanding "Originium Arts," you can't even pull the trigger.
I see... I was rather curious about it. Today my class was talking about the guardian guns they want in the future...
Do you know about "guardian guns"? In Laterano, every Sankta elementary schooler gets an actual gun when they turn twelve...!
It's honestly hard to believe... but I suppose this is what a difference in customs means. Right, I understand.
Things that amaze us are taken for granted here. Getting a gun at twelve...
Ken will be turning twelve soon too. Will you get a "guardian gun"?
No, no, no, don't think about that seriously... Besides, we aren't Sankta.
Speaking of which, didn't Ms. Carla seem a little odd today when she talked about Sankta "communicating" with guns? Like something was troubling her...
Oh, who could that be...
Surprise! Dear cousins, Miss Giada and I have come to see you.
Even going by the lie you told the Executor, you have exactly one fake cousin here.
We were only passing by, but Giulio said we could tell you about the placement arrangements in advance.
And bring you two boxes of cream puffs from the next street over, in case you hadn't discovered that perfect cream puff shop yet!
The shop on San Rocco Street? I remember you mentioning it.

Wow, you remember!
...But did I mention it to you? Why don't I remember that...
To business.
The placement schedule is already up inside the funeral home. Your placement with us starts the day after tomorrow.
Since you wrote down two related posts, you'll be with us for two days — the day after tomorrow and the day after that.
Huh, not tomorrow?
Let me see... It looks like tomorrow we go to the Confectionery Hall for the placement first, and then the funeral home...

So you'll be working at the Confectionery Hall tomorrow. I'd love to skip work and come play!
—Only joking, I won't actually skip!
As if I'd leave the whole funeral to Giada.

...?
Right, right, to business!
Miss Giada asked for you to be put on her project herself!
She may seem cold, but Miss Giada is a thoroughly attentive and considerate person.
What are you talking about? This was arranged long ago. It has nothing to do with whether I'm considerate.
Yuki, let me be clear up front: once you've finished the day's work and filled in your records, you may leave early, but you cannot simply skip out. I have to answer to my workplace as well.
That's everything. Get plenty of rest.
What? You're leaving already? We haven't even opened the cream puffs. Aren't you going to share them?
I'm the one leaving. You may stay or do whatever you like — you were the one buying the sweets anyway.
Goodbye.
I didn't dare say a word...
Woof...
Our leader and Mr. Giulio said Miss Giada was a warm and gentle person... Is she in a bad mood?
Haah... It's probably my fault. Sorry about that. I think I made Giada angry...
She's been under a lot of pressure lately...
We already had our differences at work, and then there's the placement. Student placements don't really help — they just add to the coaching and explaining.
Ah! I've put my foot in it again, haven't I? I don't mean it's your fault! Not at all! I was only trying to explain Giada's situation...
We were actually discussing the venue layout earlier. Giada explained her thinking, but in the end I still didn't want to change it...
She laughed out of sheer exasperation, and I thought my proposal had amused her, so I asked if she liked it, and then...
I meant to come see you and have some sweets together to cheer her up...
Mm... Your heart was in the right place, Mr. Giulio...
But did I handle it that badly?
Um... I wouldn't go that far. People have different temperaments and different ways of doing things...
If anything, the two of you seem to get on rather well.
Huh? Really? So she isn't angry after all?
She's definitely angry.
Haah...
But Miss Giada really did buy the cream puffs together with you, and came all the way here with you to visit us... didn't she?
Her manner was a bit cold, but if she truly disliked you, I don't think she'd be willing to do those things with you.
Haah. I don't want to keep making her angry either. It's just that on the very thing she cares about most, I can't... I don't want to give way.
I see...
Look on the bright side — in the end we both want this funeral to go well, so we're bound to make up afterward.
Arf!
Koromaru agrees too, don't you?
Don't worry about us. You've got your own troubles, haven't you? Relax, we're adults. We'll sort it out!
I should be off as well. You're at the Confectionery Hall tomorrow, right? Don't get so excited you can't sleep.
Aren't you having any cream puffs?
Ah... it's fine, you eat them. I bought them for you anyway — I won't fight children over sweets!
Anyway, take care of yourselves. See you the day after tomorrow.
Isn't the Doctor coming today?
He said that now we've confirmed Laterans can't see Shadows, the night work is ours, and we're to report any new information to him. He seems to have other work of his own.
I see. Come to think of it, there's something mysterious about the Doctor... Is he really just an ordinary teacher?
(Shakes his head)
I never thought he was an ordinary teacher.
Mm... He understood the "other world" business almost immediately, and he also came up very quickly with the idea of using Fuuka's ability to locate the door...
...Huh, what? Are you talking about me?
We're just talking about the Doctor. But you look like something's on your mind, Fuuka...?
Mm...
...When Mr. Giulio was saying goodbye this evening, it looked like you wanted to tell him something... Is it about that?
You're so perceptive, Yukari...
I really was thinking about Miss Giada and Mr. Giulio. I can't help feeling the two of them could get along...
Miss Giada is cold toward him, but I think she may be hurting too.
Not knowing how to convey how you feel, and being taken for someone who dislikes the other person... that's just too sad.
...You're so kind, Fuuka. Still, like Mr. Giulio said, they're both adults. They'll work it out. You don't have to worry so much...
Mm...
...Wait, what's that noise? I know how Laterano is by now, but making a racket like that in the middle of the night is going a bit far...!
Oh! I think it came up in class — Laterans feel a connection to the Lord in the sound of gunfire, and find peace of mind or something...
That's all very well, but isn't it far too loud? Can anyone really find peace in that...
Wait... I think I'm sensing Shadows, right up ahead! That noise might not be coming from the citizens at all — it might be Shadows running riot...!
You're kidding, Shadows...! I think the range is up ahead. They're running riot there...
I don't know if anyone's still at the range at this hour... If they get attacked it'll be terrible!
Let's hurry over and see.
Arf!
It really is Shadows...!
Something's off... Are they chasing something?
No, not chasing — is someone driving them?
...Launchers deployed!
Full salvo—!
A familiar voice came down together with a rain of shells from the sky.
Everyone looked up. A girl's figure wheeled through the rising smoke.
Hounded by the shells, the Shadows on the ground scattered and collided, seeming to scream without sound.
The blonde girl rose into the air again, and behind her a figure as august as a god spread its arms, a stalwart shield standing at her back.
Charging—
Firing!
Like a falling golden meteor, the girl tore through the eerie-colored sky and struck down hard on the Shadows herded together below!
Aigis!
Thank goodness... we've found Aigis!
Aigis, over here!
Makoto, everyone! So this is where you were...!
Thank goodness, we're finally all together...! We've been here for days now... Did you only just arrive in Laterano, Aigis?
Laterano?
Ah, we'd better explain to Aigis — so, where we are now is a country called Laterano...
—Ken, look out!!
Damn it, why are these Shadows so persistent!
...Shadows? No, these are not—
Arooo!!
They're attacking again!
Fight first. We'll go over the details back at the dorm.
...Understood!
Makoto, please give me your combat orders!
So from today, I will be attending school with everyone. Is that correct?
Yes. I reported everything that happened last night to the Doctor, and got his instructions.
He replied that it would be best for Aigis to move with us today.
But the placement starts today, doesn't it... Shouldn't Aigis go through the enrollment process first?
Mm... We have to gather at school before heading to the Confectionery Hall, so shall we ask when we get there?
I have a feeling the Doctor may have already arranged everything...
Now that you mention it, that is possible...
May we set off?
Let's go. To school.
Good morning.
Good morning. You must be Aigis!
Yes, I am Aigis.
Amiya, isn't the Doctor here?
He said he has no classes today and is catching up on sleep...
Huh... Then what about Aigis's enrollment? We're going to the Confectionery Hall for our placement today, aren't we...
Do we leave Aigis at school by herself to handle the paperwork...?
Or has the Doctor already miraculously taken care of all of it...?
At this hour the administrative office staff have only just clocked in, so I don't think even the Doctor could manage that...
No way...
But Amiya looks awfully confident about something?
Aigis, would you rather stay at school, or come to the Confectionery Hall?
I would like to move with Makoto and everyone. Besides, the Doctor appears to have instructed as much.
Then I understand.
Aigis, let's set the enrollment aside for now — just come with us to the Confectionery Hall!
Huh, can Aigis just join the placement like that?
I think I've worked out how the Doctor handles things — you remember what he said last time.
Then I understand as well.
If the Doctor were here, he'd probably say, "Since Aigis isn't a student of this school yet, where she goes is entirely up to her."
"If it's only a matter of staying together, Aigis can simply be at the Confectionery Hall as a customer."
Life in Laterano really is a life of understanding rules...
Once the placement is over, I'll buy the Doctor a sweet as thanks. Amiya, could you take it to him?
Of course. Let's get a box of cupcakes — he seems to like the ones with ladyfingers lately.
...All right then, Amiya, Yukari, you two go to the back and follow the baker's instructions.
Fuuka and Yuki will stay out front and work with the counter and service staff.
As for you two... Aigis and Ken, is it? You aren't on the placement roster...
Then, may we stay here as customers? Aigis and I, and Koromaru...
You may. Though if you're using a table, you'll have to order something~
Woof!
Placement students, remember to wear your name tags — that's what marks you as trainee staff. Now then, any questions?
...Yes. Why am I the only one changing into a whole outfit?
You have a special assignment! I've booked a cinematographer today to shoot promotional footage for the Confectionery Hall, and I need you to work with them~
Hello there, trainee. I'll be counting on you today.
You're not afraid of the camera, are you, Yuki? Don't be nervous, just work as usual. I'm after something natural and everyday...
Good morning, Kayla!
Here you are again, Idida.
Last week you promised you'd think about letting my ice cream be sold at a stall in the Hall! How's the thinking going?
Mm... Idida, today is a bit busy. Could you come another day? Here, have a box of cookies.
Kayla, do you even remember how many boxes of cookies I've taken from you by now...?
I'm not leaving today! I've brought a whole cartload of ice cream, and I'm going to make you understand the virtues of sugar-free ice cream!
Sugar-free ice cream? I am very interested.
Aigis...?
Because making ice cream necessarily requires sugar. Is that not so?
Exactly. Sugar plays a vital role in how ice cream sets — stabilizing the structure, lowering the freezing point... Whether you put sugar in ice cream isn't simply a question of taste.
"Sugar-free ice cream" is a contradiction in terms... It can't exist, and even if it did, it shouldn't be called ice cream...!
Idida, no matter how unwilling you are to admit it — ice cream cannot go without sugar!
That's old thinking! If Laterano can do without a god, why can't ice cream do without sugar?
Kayla, is it that you won't accept sugar-free ice cream because you're afraid it won't sell? Because it doesn't taste good? Or... simply because you think it isn't right?
I'm not afraid it won't sell — I develop plenty of flops myself... But "ice cream must have sugar" is absolutely not just my personal opinion!
As a neighbor, I'm happy to give little Idida's business a hand. But as the steward of this Confectionery Hall, I can't do something so careless.

And if people are willing to accept my sugar-free ice cream?
Kayla, just for today, give me one...
half a counter! If people really do like them, you'll think about my proposal again. All right?
Haah...

Aigis, Ken, Amiya and I are on our break...
Huh? What's Yuki doing?
They are holding a contest to sell ice cream.
A contest? Against whom?
A girl named Idida.
The one over there? I thought elementary schoolers couldn't join the placement...
She isn't an elementary schooler. She's an ice cream maker from nearby who wants to sell her "sugar-free ice cream" at this Confectionery Hall.
Sugar-free ice cream...? Would customers who come to a "Confectionery Hall" buy something like that?
And what she's selling right now looks like the ordinary ice cream from the stall. Or is that what sugar-free ice cream looks like?
What Idida is selling is indeed the ordinary ice cream the shop provides. The one selling the sugar-free ice cream is Makoto. Kayla said that is fairer.
She said that if the sugar-free ice cream sells well no matter who's selling it, that proves the customers like the sugar-free ice cream itself.
Pitching sugar-free ice cream to Laterans... I can't quite picture it...
I believe Kayla is very kind. She must want to grant Idida's request, which is why she arranged it this way.
Because without a doubt, Makoto will be able to sell more ice cream than Idida.
Going by how things look so far, maybe so...
Idida? Helping out at the Hall today? Get me five tubs of raspberry raisin ice cream, would you?
What...? Raisins are an extremely high-sugar food! Ice cream already has plenty of sugar in it, and if you add raisins on top the sugar content could go over thirty percent!!
A tub of this is four hundred grams, which means one tub alone could mean over a hundred and twenty grams of sugar! Five tubs is six hundred!
Anna, think about it properly. Are you really going to eat thiiiis much sugar?
Er... I eat this much every week, though?
Sugar! Is incredibly evil! It brings cavities, drowsiness, inflammation, hormone imbalances, skin aging, weight gain... It's an accomplice to every health problem there is!
Anna... won't you think about your body for a moment?
...That's her idea of a "sales pitch"...
But things look a little delicate on Yuki's side too... Is he a bit nervous?
I haven't seen these ice creams before. Are they new?
They're new.
...Aren't you going to tell me about them? It looks like a rather unusual flavor.
It's sugar-free ice cream, made with a special recipe.
And? What exactly is "special" about it?
It's healthy.
Would you like to buy some?
Ice cream that benefits the body should be highly appealing food for humans. If it were me, I would certainly buy it.
Uh-huh... huh? No, wait, you're a robot... Come to think of it, Aigis, do you have any money?
I do not have Lateran currency.
...If Makoto doesn't sell anything at all, how will his placement be graded...
Welcome.
Velliv, I never expected the dessert shop you recommended to be a neighborhood market like this...
I thought Miss Ensia would prefer this sort of place.
You're quite right, I like it here! Is there a dessert you'd recommend, Velliv?
I'm fond of the fig ice cream here.
Let me see, the ice cream is over...
Hello.
Buying ice cream? I recommend the sugar-free ice cream over there!
The sugar-free ice cream is on this side.
Which side is the fig ice cream on?
Right, that's mine... Oh, I'm sorry! It's already sold out.
I see... Then is that sugar-free ice cream you mentioned any good?
...Sugar-free ice cream? How did Kayla allow such a thing here?
What do you mean, "such a thing"?! Sugar-free ice cream is the greatest innovation in Lateran history!
Miss Ensia, if you wish to learn about Lateran specialties, I'd suggest considering other options.
I came here to learn more about Laterano as it is now. I'm very interested in a "great innovation."
I'll take all of this sugar-free ice cream! Can you pack it up?
I can. Thank you for your purchase.
...It really all sold? Every bit of the sugar-free ice cream?
Yes, Kayla!
And the regular ice cream stock? Idida, you didn't pull any tricks, did you? Let me look at the ledger...
Oh~ quite a lot of that sold too! Looking at it this way, it seems to be a draw...
...Haah! No matter how I explain the harms of sugar, everyone just buys those high-sugar sweets anyway.
Why won't anyone believe sugar is bad... All the Columbian papers I found say so!
I don't know anything about Columbian papers... but how could a Lateran give up sweets, Idida?
We grew up eating them.

You know madeleines are my favorite, don't you? That's because after I got my guardian gun, my first live-fire practice left me terribly dizzy, and the sweet my mother had ready for me was a madeleine.
I'll always remember the sweetness spreading through my mouth as I chewed that cake.
Sweetness is a taste, but it's also our lives and our memories...
However great the upheaval, as long as those memories are there, a Lateran's life won't change so easily...
We'll still love sweets, and I'll still have a madeleine after shooting practice.
Idida, you want people to come to love your sugar-free ice cream, yet you turn a blind eye to what they love right now. Is that really all right?
...Kayla, I...
Ms. Kayla, have you tried Idida's ice cream?
I bought a few and set them aside, to share with my friends...
Would you like to try one? I thought it tasted rather good.
Mm...
Huh... This isn't like the tasting before? Only a little, but there really is some sweetness...

Yes... I tried a sugar-free sweetener... It's so hard to get hold of! You have to order it from abroad, and only one logistics company that opened recently will deliver it...
It still doesn't taste quite like sugar, so I didn't think there was any need to add much, but...
Well, at least it works as a new flavor of sugar-free ice cream...
The contest ended in a draw, but the sugar-free ice cream really did sell out.
All right. If the point was to prove that "some people will accept sugar-free ice cream," then this is certainly enough...
Idida, let's find a time to talk through the details of renting a counter.

Kayla...! Thank you...
And you too, sir... "Makoto," is that how you say it?
Thank you as well!
Please take my card — if you and your friends want more sugar-free ice cream, you can order by mail, delivery included!
All right, the placement hours are nearly up. Students, take out your terminals and I'll sign off.
Zita, did you get any good shots?
Better than expected! I even ran into that famous athlete here...
Athlete? Who?
The one who saved sugar-free ice cream~
Miss Ensia, I understand your curiosity. But not everything is connected to Laterano's transformation, and sugar-free ice cream certainly isn't.
Asking me to "share all this with friends" puts me in a difficult position.
Huh? I wasn't thinking that deeply about it. The ice cream really is rather good...
And you needn't watch me so closely. I know what I said to you before... but the truth is I came here for my own selfish reasons.
I only wanted to see how Laterans live now... After all, our situations are somewhat alike these days, aren't they?
Is that what you were thinking?

It is, that's exactly what I was thinking...
Oh, is that a sporting goods shop up ahead?
Miss Ensia, sporting goods in Laterano refers to—
Haah. Looking after a girl this guileless is its own kind of trouble.
So much ice cream... I wonder if young Lemuen's logistics company handles frozen goods...
(Quietly) If that good-for-nothing were here, I could just dump the lot on him to eat.
...Don't go dying out there.
I rested before we set out to investigate today, so I feel much better...
Though I've been thinking about what Aigis said earlier, about those "Shadows"...
Yes. They do resemble Shadows somewhat, but I believe they are definitely not Shadows. At the very least, they differ from the Shadows of our world.
So I think we might consider another name for them. How about simply "monsters"? Simpler and clearer.
Mm, that's true. I called them that before because their readings had things in common with Shadows... but it's better to distinguish them.
Since Aigis has confirmed they aren't Shadows, let's call them monsters.
But... if they aren't Shadows, does our earlier guess that "the monsters may have come to Laterano through the door like us" still hold?
I'd been hoping we could find the door by investigating them...
And even though we met up with Aigis last night, we still didn't see the door...
The Doctor raised that point too when I contacted him. But...
We aren't destroying these monsters only for our own sake.
Right. We still haven't figured out what kind of harm the monsters do to Laterans...
Yesterday at the range, Aigis saw another case of a monster making contact with a Lateran.
That is correct. The Laterans were very friendly.

To drive the monsters off I had no choice but to use thermal weaponry in front of civilians, and rather than taking cover, some of them applauded me and said my gun-handling approach and costume technique were highly distinctive.

No, let's set that part aside for now...
I remember you said that while evacuating people, someone accidentally touched a monster and passed right through the middle of it. That happened, didn't it?
Correct. Such a thing did occur.
And did anything... happen to that person?
The woman with feathers afterward handed me her weapon and said she envied me greatly.
I do not understand. Could she have envied my gun-handling approach and costume technique?
However, since she had contacted a monster, I monitored her physical condition. She did not appear to be injured.

The Doctor... is that impressive? Is that really something an ordinary teacher could do in a few days...
I asked him the same thing. He said it was "because I have reliable friends helping"...
Only, as for finding the door, we really have lost our direction a bit...
...Even though Aigis confirming those monsters aren't Shadows makes it less likely they came to Laterano through the door...
I've been thinking, though... their presence really is very like a Shadow's.
Yes. If we are speaking of similarity, it certainly exists.

Doesn't this sight look terribly familiar...

Yes. If our earlier assumption was wrong, at least we've ruled out one wrong direction.

Woof woof, woof!
Thank you for agreeing with me, Koromaru.
Koromaru is saying it is strange that no enemies have appeared at all.

The Shadow readings I'm picking up...

...Awoo!
Koromaru says there is a suspicious smell over there.
Is that a broken-down confessional? Koromaru, didn't the two of us come out of a confessional on our first day? They're very common in Laterano.
Still, with a facility damaged like this, shouldn't we report it to an Executor once it's daytime...
Woof woof!

Arooo—woof—!
Koromaru says — that is not an ordinary confessional—

—Woof!
...So this is where we're doing our placement today? I think it was called the Ecclesia Requietum Funeral Home... This is where Miss Giada and Mr. Giulio work, isn't it—
(Yawn) Haah...

Ah...

I hope today's placement goes smoothly. And I hope those two don't argue again today...

The focus of the work is different.
Don't interrupt, Giulio. Explaining this part is my job.
Sorry...
It feels somewhat improper to tell children all this... but you chose to do your placement here yourselves, so I won't be making allowances for your feelings.
If you're putting this down as a career interest, then what follows is what you ought to know.
Do you know the difference between burial and cremation?
Interred in earth, interred in fire — different ways of handling the deceased's remains... What differences are there beyond that?
From a funeral professional's point of view, the two are worlds apart. Cost, time required, how complex the process is, what public facilities they demand... none of it is comparable.
Laterano's traditional funerary practice centers on burial conducted through the Ecclesia Requietum system, with other methods as supplements.

At the fixed stops along the city of Laterano's original route, each district had its own Ecclesia Requietum handling matters including funerals and cemetery management... That system is still running today.
And this funeral home... will be the beginning of Laterano bringing cremation to scale within the nomadic city itself.
...Cremation inside the nomadic city... then how do you visit a grave...?
The funeral home will have a place to hold the remains, so people can come and remember. Memorial gatherings can be held here as well.
...In other words, the funeral home serves as the cemetery for those who choose cremation...
Miss Giada, you mentioned that Laterano's traditional method is burial. The first Ecclesia Requietum Funeral Home... if I may ask, why build a facility like this now?

Miss Giada, may I speak now?
No.
Just one sentence?

...You've never mentioned that.
I still haven't finished unpacking.
—Is that supposed to be a reason? Never mind... Your private affairs can wait.
Does anyone have questions about the funeral home, based on what I've covered?
...Miss Giada, you said the funeral home hasn't opened officially yet. So what work will we be doing now?

Ready, kids?
Hosting a party again?

Laterano really is much more convenient. The funeral home routes things very efficiently, even though the department was only just set up...
I have a question.
Go ahead!

Choosing the venue, designing the order of events, preparing facilities and materials, planning and inviting the guests, arranging catering and music...
The party I'm throwing and the funeral Giada is responsible for are, on a physical level, one and the same thing.

Right? Right? But Giada keeps insisting on drawing a line between the two.
Haah...

You really are worried about Giada and me.

A new funerary practice, a Liberi funeral planner, and whether this funeral home can be accepted by Laterans at all.

Does a funeral have to be silent and solemn? A funeral is also an occasion when many people come together. Why can't it be a chance to enjoy the present moment together?
Is that the thinking behind adding a karaoke relay to the latter half of the funeral?
Oh dear, when did you get back...
From "whether a new funerary practice and a Liberi funeral planner can be accepted by Laterans."
Of course, you're right. That is exactly what this funeral is. And you're doing all of this to help me — that's what you want to say, isn't it?

Which is why you removed the cremation witnessing and bone-gathering I had scheduled there?

Wow... Giada, you're a genius?! That's so much better than the karaoke relay. You really are the professional!

Don't.

Doctor...

Come with me to buy a coffee.

I don't know how you've been interpreting the friction between Giulio and me...

I'm glad you talked Giulio out of that ash salute yesterday... He would have made everyone there look like lunatics.

Even if it once did, it shouldn't now.

Because it's useless. Every time we "discuss" something you say you'll weigh it, you'll think about it — and then what?

Giada... I— I don't understand your expression. Could you just tell me?

In Columbia, the only person I could feel empathy with was my father. He was a man forever full of worries...
A worry-ridden Sankta — rare, isn't it? Maybe that's why he left Laterano.
To cheer him up, I studied no end of jokes and tricks!
For me, that was when empathy was most useful. I could feel his mood genuinely lifting...

I often thought it wasn't the jokes that amused him. It was that he could feel, from the bottom of his heart, that I was well and that I wanted him to be happy — and so a little of his worry lifted...
Hm, maybe my aunt noticed I was good at making people happy when I was small, and that's why she left that will!
A cheerful Lateran would want everyone to enjoy themselves at their own funeral too, wouldn't they?
So... even if Giada's thinking makes sense, there are some things I want to hold out for.
...We've already lost so much. If we're then crushed by grief and can't pull ourselves out, that isn't Laterano.

Miss Giada, ready yet? Still not?

...Should I put makeup on her... For this funeral...

What do you say, Makoto?

Mr. Giulio still keeps up that light-hearted manner, but I'm starting to feel that the two of them are both entirely serious...
...This morning, when I went to ask Miss Giada about the case, I learned some things.
About what divides them... and about the great upheaval Laterano went through not long ago.
Perhaps that's what the Doctor meant by "the changes Laterano is going through."
...What exactly happened?
Laterano's "god" died only a few months ago...
...That something like that happened...
If that is so, then what divides Miss Giada and Mr. Giulio is not merely a matter of taste.
It is that both believe this funeral carries a special meaning in Laterano as it is now, yet their convictions are utterly different.
And Laterano building a facility like this funeral home, and trying to change funerary customs, must be connected to that as well...
The reason they both take this funeral so seriously is probably that it's how each of them faces the Laterano of today...
And that's why you didn't step into their argument today, isn't it, Makoto?
Yes.
And there's another question I've been turning over...
About those Shadow-like monsters.

Because the god died, monsters appeared...?
Yes. And you remember, don't you — the Doctor was very interested in the "monster shaped like a confessional," and had us write up the other monsters' forms too.

That may be so, but there's a great deal tied to us as well...

We'll only know by investigating further...
Fuuka?
Nn...

What? Near the dorm?!

Woof...!
Then let's move. We have to find where it is.
It's here...

But its position never changed during that time... It should be somewhere around here.
...Would anyone still be at the funeral home at this hour...
Let's check. The monster didn't hide inside the funeral home, did it?
(Shakes her head) If it had only gone inside a building I'd still sense it, especially a presence that strong...
How strange... Could it already have been destroyed? Is there someone besides us who can destroy them?
That's unlikely... Nothing like this has ever happened before.
Going by everything we've found so far, we should be the only ones in Laterano who can destroy the monsters...
A reading that strong — why would it just vanish...?
The area around the funeral home is far quieter than other blocks, and in the still night footsteps carried clearly.

What are you doing here? Coming to the funeral home at this hour... and armed?
Uh... um... we were training at the range just now! On the way back to the dorm we remembered we'd left something here...
Training this late? I doubt the dorm has a curfew, but staying out this long isn't good for you either.
Well... tomorrow's a day off, so we thought just a little...
What about you, Miss Giada? Working this late...?
Mm.
Miss Giada, did you see anything lying around?
Ah... I wouldn't know. If you dropped something, go and look. The side door is open. Help yourselves.
Arf...
This is probably nothing... but Miss Giada, did you see anything strange nearby? Or hear any unusual sounds... anything like that?
No.

Miss Giada, what were you doing just now?
